utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-03-67-PT, the Prosecutor versus Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Mr. Seselj. Can you follow what I am saying in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, for now, but from previous experience, I know that sometimes I'm unable to follow because of poor interpretation. However, at present, I can, yes. But I will tell you when I am no longer able to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please do. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. I'm Daniel Saxon, together with my colleague, Ulrich Mussemeyer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And good morning to you. I understand, Mr. Seselj, that you are defending yourself. You chose to defend yourself. But as you know, we have appointed Mr. Aleksandar Lazarevic, who I recognise here in the room, in the courtroom. Good morning to you, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I'm Aleksandar Lazarevic, assigned standby counsel for Professor Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. First thing I wanted to state is that there has been a change in the composition of the Trial Chamber, and that's because Judge Schomburg has moved on to the Appeals Chamber. I have taken over the presidency of the Trial Chamber, and for the time being and until the -- your case comes to trial, the Pre-Trial Chamber composition is as follows: Me as the Presiding Judge, then there is Judge Florence Mumba, and Judge Jean-Claude Antonetti. I am also the Pre-Trial Judge for the whole duration of the pre-trial stage, unless there is a change at some point in time. The last Status Conference was held on the 3rd of July of 2003, and as required by Rule 65 bis, we are summoning this Status Conference within the 120-day period. The purpose of Status Conferences is, as you know, to organise exchanges between the parties, to ensure an expeditious preparation for the trial, and also to give the accused the opportunity to raise any matter related to his mental health or general health or physical condition, as well as to the conditions of detention in the Detention Unit in Scheveningen, if there are any complaints in that area. I suggest we start with the first item of the agenda, which is -- relates to issues relating to disclosure. I will state first what is the information that I am in possession of. And if there are then comments, additions, remarks, or suggestions from either of you on this matter, then please you will take the floor as I ask you. Why is the microphone of the accused switched on? It should be switched on when -- when I give him the floor. Okay. So the first matter is issues relating to disclosure. And I will deal first with disclosure of exculpatory material, which is regulated by Rule 68 of our Rules. At the last Status Conference on the 3rd of July, that is, the Prosecution disclosed the first -- the first batch of exculpatory material to the accused, and all the materials were in the Serbo-Croat language. The accused accepted these documents or acknowledged the receipt of these documents. I -- it seems to me that the question arose as to whether the -- any Rule 68 material that is not in the B/C/S language should be provided to the accused in B/C/S, in Serbo-Croat. It has been put to me that the Prosecution stated at the time that it would continue to identify Rule 68 material and disclose it but that it was not prepared or willing to translate that material into B/C/S, as this would be too great a burden to bear. And it also results to me that the accused on this matter stated that he could not work in English and that neither of his two legal assistants can understand English and that he kept insisting that every document provided to him must and should be in the B/C/S language. Let's start with this Rule 68 material for the time being and leave the Rule 66 disclosure until later. What is the position now from the Prosecutors -- the Prosecution side?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Effectively the position of the Prosecution has not changed, and I'd simply like to make a point of clarification in -- in our position regarding the potential burden of having to translate potentially exculpatory material from English or another language into the language of the accused. Actually, the point of the Prosecution was not that this would be a burden too great for the Prosecution to bear but actually would be a burden too great for CLSS, the Translation Unit in the Registry to bear, and that is simply our understanding from our communications with that section of this Tribunal. We have today, Your Honour, to provide to the accused, with hopefully the assistance of the Registry, another packet of material. It is all in the language -- first language of the accused, Bosnian/Serbian/Croat, and we also have a videotape which we had previously provided to the accused under Rule 68 but which Dr. Seselj was unable to play on the apparatus available to him in the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. There is a motion which refers to that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So we have recreated hopefully a more workable copy, and we have that ready to give to him today. As well, Your Honour, on the issue of material that is not in the language of the accused, of course, I'm referring to material subject to disclosure under Rule 68, the Prosecution is hopeful that it might be able to provide this material to the standby counsel so that the standby counsel could at least advise the accused, Dr. Seselj, as to the existence and the nature of this material. And that would be the Prosecution's suggestion this morning to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Professor Seselj, do you have any comments on Rule 68 disclosure material, or Rule 68 material?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I already filed a submission in which I informed you that I'm also prepared to perform my obligations under Rule 68. As my advisors were very successful --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, Rule 67.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I have prepared some 300 pages of evidence and to this I add 80 published books of mine containing all my speeches in the parliaments of Serbia and Yugoslavia, all my newspaper interviews, all my interviews to radio and television stations, some court proceedings and most of my public speakings at public rallies. I think that this will be a lot of work for the Prosecution, but it is a complete set of materials after which they may perhaps withdraw their indictment. As the OTP is handing over to me exculpatory material at the Status Conference, I also have the right to hand over the materials I have under Rule 67(A)(ii), as regards exculpatory and every other material, it has to be disclosed to me in the Serbian language and I insist this. I will never change my position on this. As for the alleged standby counsel, Aleksandar Lazarevic, this is a very serious problem. And, Your Honour, I have to tell you that tomorrow I will institute criminal proceedings because some crimes were committed when Aleksandar Lazarevic was appointed. This is something that was agreed on when (redacted) (redacted), spent (redacted) holidays in the house of attorney Toma Fila on Lake Ohrid. And through (redacted), Toma Fila communicated with Hans Holthuis, the Registrar, and this is when it was agreed that Aleksandar Lazarevic should be appointed as my standby counsel. Why cannot Aleksandar Lazarevic participate in my defence in any way? Because Toma Fila was the attorney for Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, in legal proceedings against me in 1993 and 1994. On that occasion, Aleksandar Lazarevic was an intern in the office of Toma Fila. I have prepared here my book, which contains the entire documents on the court proceedings instituted and that had to do with me and Arkan. And Fila acted as counsel for Arkan. Secondly, I have also discovered criminal actions in which Hans Holthuis is involved to distribute the money, the funds set aside by the Tribunal for defence between Hans Holthuis, (redacted), and perhaps other people. And 21 attorneys from Toma Fila's office are now actively engaged in 15 proceedings before this Tribunal. I have been in a conflict with Toma Fila and his entire office for more than a decade. Toma Fila was one of the founders of Arkan's Party of Serbian Unity, and the Prosecution is not happy that Maja Gojkovic should be one of my counsel, because she was a founder of a political party, but they don't mind that Toma Fila was also the founder of a political party. Also, I had a conflict with Slavko Jerkovic -- or rather, with the father of Aleksandar Lazarevic, Ljubisa Lazarevic, who is a professor in the faculty of law in Belgrade, and he publicly attacked Professor Ratko Markovic for writing a positive paper about me, a positive report about me when I was up for election as a -- as a professor. I was illegally driven away from that faculty later. The father of Aleksandar Lazarevic is notorious as a professor who -- who falsifies students' exams. He shares an office with Ilija Drazic. Attorney Ilija Drazic is the -- an advisor of the Mafia minister, Goran Pitic. And furthermore, the wife of Aleksandar Lazarevic is a high-ranking official Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of the present Mafia regime in Serbia, her name is Aleksandra [phoen] Lazarevic, and she is the public attorney there. I will, therefore, institute criminal proceedings because of all these things, and I advise you that never under any circumstances will I agree to have any kind of contact with Aleksandar Lazarevic. I have my legal advisors in whom I have unbounded confidence who are already helping me in my defence, although Hans Holthuis is trying to avoid them at any cost and although the OTP is perhaps afraid of having -- me having Maja Gojkovic as my legal advisor. But that's their problem. She fulfils all the conditions to be my legal advisor. My legal advisor does not have to speak English and I will not be speaking to them in English. They will only be speaking to me. But I insist that they sit next to me in the courtroom so they can assist me during the proceedings, that they can at least turn the pages of documents for me if I ask them to do that. Your Honour, this is as regards that matter. But now I wish to have it entered into the record that -- that my book, "Sudanije Nepokojnog Vojvode" should be entered here. It contains many of the legal proceedings instituted against me by the regime in Serbia including the one involving Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, where Arkan was defended by Toma Fila with his office and Aleksandar Lazarevic, attorney at law, was his intern at the time. Also,"Osmanlijski Sejmeni Na Provnom Fakultetski," which concerns the scandals at the faculty of law in connection with my expulsion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Saxon, do you have any objection at all at Mr. Seselj presenting or tendering his -- his book at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: To disclosing the book to the Prosecution, the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He contends that it is exculpatory, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We have no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just a point of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. If you -- if you want to add something, please. I'm sorry for interrupting you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Just a point of clarification for the accused. Rule 67, as it's written, refers to special defences, Your Honour, in particular the defence of alibi or diminished responsibility. And the Prosecution hasn't heard anything that indicates that these books that Dr. Seselj is tendering this morning really deal with these issues. But having said that, given that this -- this is an under -- an unrepresented accused, we are certainly willing to accept it at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you, Mr. Saxon. Professor Seselj, you -- I had asked you to restrict your comments to Rule 68 material disclosure, and you put in several other matters with which we'll deal later. As far as Rule 68 material is concerned, I take it that the position, if it's -- if I were to crystallise it now, is that there is a further batch today that is being disclosed to you and that is in a language that you understand and, therefore, there is no problem as far as today is concerned. When we come to the stage that the Prosecution -- when the Prosecution wants to disclose Rule 68 material, which is not in a language that you can understand, you have the right to file a proper motion, address it to the Tribunal via the Registrar, and we will decide there and then whether this material needs to be translated into a language that you can understand or not. But at the present moment, today, the matter does not arise because what is being disclosed today is in your own language. That's number one. Number two, the question of the appointment of Mr. Lazarevic. That is the responsibility of the Trial Chamber. It's the Trial Chamber that has appointed Mr. Lazarevic. You have every right to refuse audience to Mr. Lazarevic. You have every right not to even look at his face. You have every right to think what you think, what you would like to think about Mr. Lazarevic, but he is there and he is going to remain there as standby counsel, as per our decision of -- of May of this year. As regards your intention to institute "legal criminal proceedings," do as you please. We'll see what these criminal proceedings that you are referring to are and there -- if they have a place inside the agenda of the pre-trial stage, then we will -- we will discuss that. Otherwise, I am not prepared to discuss those matters as -- since I am not yet seized with those matters, you having not "instituted these criminal proceedings." With regard also to instituting criminal proceedings against the -- our Registrar, Mr. Hans Holthuis, do as you please. Again, this does not form part of the agenda of today's Pre-Trial Conference, and I don't know if it will ever form part of any agenda of any Pre-Trial Conference. If it does, then we will discuss it. As regards any material that you would like to disclose today to the Prosecution, to the Court, which you think is exculpatory, make sure that it is exculpatory and you're free to -- to tender it. Although, I need to advise you that it is very strange that at this stage an accused assisted or unassisted takes that stand. But it's up to you. I'm not going to interfere with your wishes if you want to tender those books or any of them, you're free to do so. So the last thing is about disclosure of Rule 68 material at a later stage. We'll deal with that matter as and when it arises. And it -- I will deal with it only if there is an ad hoc motion, be it verbal or -- or written. But as far as today's sitting is concerned, the question does not arise. Rule 66 material. Do I have a confirmation from you, Mr. Saxon or Mr. Mussemeyer, that Rule 66 disclosure -- material disclosure is complete?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. In part that is because the Prosecution is awaiting a decision from the Trial Chamber based on -- related to a motion that was filed in September of this year, related to certain protective measures. It --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Stop there for a time being. Professor Seselj, on the 15th of September, the Prosecution filed a motion, which was dated 10th of September but which was filed five days later. I have information that it was handed to you on the 17th of September. In this motion, the Prosecution is asking the Trial Chamber to authorise them not to disclose to you -- not to disclose to you certain information as is provided by Rule 66(A)(ii), which I suppose, since you have opted to defend yourself, you are familiar with. But if you don't have the Rules available before you now, in front of you,-- the problem is this, that usually one would have expected you to have replied to that motion, having received it on the 17th of September. To my knowledge, no reply has been forthcoming. I haven't received anything. If you have filed anything, please let me know. If you haven't filed anything, please tell me whether you intend to file a reply, a response to that motion, in which case even though the time limit has lapsed, I am prepared to give you a further term, time limit within which you can file your response.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As that is a question that is being addressed at the Status Conference, I am prepared to provide you with an oral reply. I don't have the intention of providing a written submission, because I have had very bad experience to date. I would write a very lengthy text, and then they would try to return it to me by all possible means. So I will be concise and provide you with an oral answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Professor Seselj, you have every right, and I appreciate that you are not ignoring my -- my appeal to you to respond to this motion, and I appreciate that you are going to economise everybody's time by responding verbally today. However, since you are bringing up a matter that has been -- has proved a problem to you and also a problem to us, and that is the length of -- of your written submissions, and since we will be seeing each other more often and on a regular basis, I suggest we Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. try to understand each other a little bit better. The Rules of this Tribunal are binding on you, on the Prosecution, and on me and the other Judges. No one has the right to go beyond or not to apply the Rules that have been created. And the Rules plus the directives that are in existence in virtue -- by virtue of the Rules specify the length that each motion, each document that is filed by either of the parties must observe. There are instances when the party, whoever it is - Prosecution or Defence - needs more space, more pages, and in that case an ad hoc motion -- application is made to the Trial Chamber, and if the Trial Chamber is justified that there is a case for more pages, it will authorise. There are many instances where all Trial Chambers have authorised submissions -- written submissions in excess of the norm. But the Rule and the directive must first be observed. When you file a motion taking the law in your hand, deciding that you need 300 pages and not 10 to present your case or to present a motion, ignoring what the Rules say, what the directives say, and ignoring what the Trial Chamber is bound by, then you're only making it difficult for yourself. So my suggestion to you is you have assumed the responsibility of defending yourself, which is a great responsibility, and you will be respected not only as an accused but also as an accused who has taken in addition the burden of defending himself. But that doesn't give you the right that no lawyer has; it doesn't give you the right that no one else has. And therefore, please stick to the Rules. If you need more pages, let us know and we will decide whether it's the case of authorising you or not. That's number one. But please now let's go back to your verbal or oral response to the Prosecution's motion of the 17th of September and stick to that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm bound by the Statute of the Tribunal and by the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, providing the provisions are not contrary to the Statute, since the Statute has precedence. And instructions from the Presiding Judge can't be a legal act which is binding because it can be binding for Judges, for court officials, et cetera. But for me as an accused, these instructions can't be legally binding. And I insist on this. This is a legal matter that no one can respond to. The Presiding Judge cannot say -- cannot limit the amount of pages I can submit, especially if I am -- if we're talking about an objection to the indictment. That is my absolute right. And I assume that in your judicial system this is true too. No one can prevent me from -- to the indictment, especially not by arguing that my submission is too lengthy. This is quite scandalous from a legal point of view, as far as this problem is concerned. On the basis of the experience of all the proceedings before this Tribunal to date, I know that in each case of concealing the identity of a victim I am concealing -- I am covering up a false witness. In the case of Milan Babic, who was a protected witness and later on his identity was disclosed, at the proceedings against Slobodan Milosevic he mentioned my name and he lied. He said that Marko Negovanovic, the minister of defence, gave him a helicopter to visit the Knin battlefield. At that time, Marko Negovanovic wasn't a minister; Tomislav Simic was. I received a helicopter from General Vukovic, the commander of the Knin Corps. And I didn't go to Belgrade with it but I went to Mostar and then to Podgorica. So the question is why is the identity of a witness concealed? In my case, not a single witness is at risk. If I have a false witness who I will make appear before this Tribunal, that's a risk. Each witness has to bear such a risk. The Prosecution has to take this risk too. The Prosecution which appeals to false testimony. So there is no risk for witnesses. But there is another danger: The Prosecution here suggests that my identity should be disclosed and that before the witness appears before the Tribunal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because there is -- either you're saying something that doesn't make sense or the interpretation that I have received doesn't make sense. I have here, but there is another danger. "The Prosecution here suggests that my identity" - that's your identity, in other words - "should be disclosed and that the witness appears before the Tribunal." Did you say that or -- I don't know. This is what I have here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The identity would be disclosed to me, the identity of a witness ten days earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what it says in the Prosecution's submission, and that Aleksandar Lazarevic will know about this identity a month in advancement. So do you know what the danger is in this case? Since Aleksandar Lazarevic is a member of Arkan's Mafia and that Mafia could eliminate a witness since they have enough time at their disposal and in that case the Prosecution could then accuse me of having eliminated a witness because of his testimony. I guarantee that if these proceedings are correct from the point of view of not obstructing my defence, as has been done so far, in that case no one will hurt a single witness, nothing will happen to any witnesses. In Belgrade and Serbia, I've had -- I have been the subject of about 50 proceedings so far. And nothing has happened to any witnesses. Even false witnesses have not been at risk because I've had experience with false witnesses before. You know as an opponent to the regime I was often present in courtrooms and I almost feel uneasy when there is a long pause, I'm so used to such things. As a matter of principle, I am against concealing the identity of a witness or anyone's testimony. And in the nature of criminal acts that are attributed to me shows that there is no need to conceal the identity of a witness, because what can this witness testify about, that I ordered that he should commit a criminal offence? I didn't have any command responsibilities. That I encouraged such a person, that's the substance of the indictment. But why should a witness whom I encouraged, why should his identity be concealed? And if you think I'm going to bring in false witnesses and that I can't prepare to demonstrate that they're not credible, what does this mean? Are you afraid of their testimony? I'm addressing the Prosecution. So there are no persuasive reasons, no convincing reasons to conceal the identity of witnesses. Furthermore, it is stated here that the identity of a witness is concealed from my defence team, my assistants, my legal assistants. I have quite a number of people who are working for me. And what does this mean? I can't inform in good time that such and such a witness is going to appear to testify about certain matters? Then we won't be able to see what there is behind his testimony and try to refute it. I don't have the conditions to what -- so if you insist on these matters and you are not ready for the trial by the year 2005, how can we proceed? You're only obstructing matters, talking about standby lawyers. You're maltreating them this way and that way. I have accepted to talk to you, but you are establishing conditions. You're saying that Maja Gojkovic can't be present as my legal assistant. What sort of a condition is that? This doesn't happen anywhere in the world. Are you to select the person who is assist me in my defence? Do you have any suspicions about her? In that case, issue an indictment against her. You suspect every Serb; I'm well aware of this fact, anyone who doesn't suit you, anyone who will not divide his fee with Hans Holthuis, you doubt -- you have do -- doubts about that person. So Your Honour, in principle I am against concealing the identity of all witnesses, and especially in this case I insist that even if you should decide that someone's identity should be concealed, this person's identity should be disclosed to me in good time so that I can prepare to refute this testimony and so that my legal assistants could be in a situation to provide me with efficient help. Otherwise, such testimony would have no purpose. A witness could appear here and say whatever he wanted to say and I would not have a possibility -- the possibility of attempting to refute this testimony. Naturally, there would be quite a few witnesses of yours for whom I will not be able to prepared. As soon as I enter here, it won't be necessary for me to prepare anything, because I will be able to reveal them immediately, to expose them immediately. There may be people who will be professionally prepared to give false testimony, and in such cases I need some time to prepare myself. I need to talk to my legal assistants over the phone, and this has not been allowed. Recently, as the investigating judge interviewed me in Belgrade -- from Belgrade about Djindjic's murder, no indictment was issued because there was no proof. Maja Gojkovic and Slavko Jerkovic were with me and they talked to me in the presence of a court official. And when I said that I was not allowed to provide them with the material that the Prosecution had provided me with, and this material was not confidential - I have three or four binders of material that can be shown to the public - I was prevented from doing this. And instead of the Prosecution telling me why this was prohibited, they tell me that it's not true that that's what the court official told me. It was someone else. It was not a Prosecution official; it was a court official. Why should I make such a distinction? It's no point. I need someone to inform me with the authority of the judicial system, whether it's a court official or a Prosecution official. I didn't provide this material. Although, I wanted to provide this material so that we could prepare ourselves correctly for my defence. The indictment is not substantial and you are not in a position to confront my defence. This document shows that you are afraid of these Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. criminal proceedings, of these judicial proceedings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Professor Seselj. There are three points that I need to address rising out of -- or four points rising out of your response. Number one is -- I've taken note of the points raised by you, namely that you are objecting on principle against the -- even the adoption of the system of non-disclosure of witnesses' names and statements and that you gave the reasons for -- for this, both general -- from a general point of view, as well as from a personal standpoint. I've taken note of those. I have also taken note of the submission that you have made that should the Trial Chamber decide for the motion of the Prosecution, you would still insist on being given notice of the name and details of -- of these witnesses in time to enable you to prepare adequately for your defence, which is a measure that has been adopted by this Tribunal on several occasions and which I see you are already aware of. So the decision on your motion will be handed down in due course as early as possible, but I must advise you that we haven't started working on it precisely because I didn't know what position Professor Seselj was going to adopt in regard. And I preferred to wait to see whether he was going to file a response or not before proceeding with the elaboration of -- of the decision. It was mentioned earlier on with regard to Rule 68 disclosure, and I also extended to Rule 66 disclosure that the Trial Chamber will certainly not be satisfied with disclosure to the standby counsel in substitution of disclosure to the accused. That would not be acceptable to me. The standby counsel has got his terms or his functions spelled out in our 9th May decision, but he is not representing the accused and certainly he is not substituting him in the role of having a right to -- for disclosure of documents under 66 and 68. So having said that, I think I don't need to state any more. Here is the other question: I am used to a system whereby we don't allow the parties to address each other directly; rather, that all submissions and all remarks pass through the Presiding Judge. I apologise to you if I allowed the accused to address you directly. I did so because I saw no objection on your part. If you have an objection to this, it's no big deal; I will just give a solution to -- to the accused. He can address you through me, although not directly. But it's -- usually we resort to that system in order to avoid confrontation, and there shouldn't be across-the-floor submissions, address -- one party addressing the other across the floor, not through the Presiding Judge. So I would like you, if you have not nothing against it, to stick to this rule, which I like to adopt in my -- in my chamber, in my courtroom. In future, Professor Seselj, if you want to address -- say something to -- to the Defence -- to the Prosecution, just tell me, "Dear Judge, I have something, a message for the Prosecution." But say it to me, instead of looking straight into their face, as if you are in a direct confrontation. Let's have some rules of the game that we adopt, because it will be easier for everyone. And as -- as I said, it will make me happier and it will make your life and their life easier, as well as mine. The last part was this: I am aware that during the last Status Conference you did raise the matter that you wanted to speak -- you offered to speak to the Office of the Prosecutor but this offer was declined. The information that I have is that there was a refusal on your part - when I say "your part," I mean the office, not you, Mr. Saxon, or whatever - and the reason being the presence of one -- either the standby counsel or legal advisor that Professor Seselj wanted to be present. I had no intention of addressing it today because I had no indication that it was going to be raised again. But once this matter has been raised, I think I am duty-bound to explore it further. Do I take it Professor Seselj - just tell me yes or no - that you still would like to have an audience with the Office of the Prosecutor to discuss some matters? Just tell me yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't just say yes or no. I could answer your question in three sentences, if that is appropriate. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Three sentences, one page each.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the first Status Conference, I was taken to Carla Del Ponte, the chief Prosecutor, who offered that I speak to the Prosecution. I said, "Very well, but provided that it is an official discussion. It should be recorded and my legal assistants should be present," et cetera. And she replied - and this is still the same sentence, as far as my language is concerned - she said that is how it would be. My objection that I raised at the last Status Conference - and this is the second sentence - is that many months had passed and we still hadn't arranged for a conversation, for a discussion. Then the Prosecution said that they were waiting for the standby lawyer. I don't know why they were waiting for him, because I will never accept -- discuss anything in his presence. And when I provided a written answer to the Prosecution, an answer to their summons and to their date of the 24th, 25th, and 26th of September, saying that I was accepting the call to a conversation and that my assistants, Maja Gojkovic and Slavko Jerkovic should be present, my lawyers from Serbia. The Prosecution then said they had nothing against Slavko Jerkovic, but that Maja Gojkovic couldn't be present. If Maja Gojkovic is not going to be allowed to be present, there's no point to the discussion. I hope that I haven't used up more than three sentences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, after the last Status Conference, the Prosecution began to make inquiries and arrangements so that it could schedule an appointment with Dr. Seselj in the Detention Unit so that an interview, a formal interview with Dr. Seselj could commence. We -- the Prosecution then received a letter from Dr. Seselj indicating that the accused wished to have Mr. Jerkovic and Ms. Gojkovic present with him, and also indicated to us that he would not be able to participate in an interview in any case until he received some routine medical treatment that had been scheduled. So the Prosecution replied that - and this is all on the record; I believe the Chamber is aware of the Prosecution's objections to the participation of Ms. Gojkovic in this process - but we were also informed that the routine medical treatment that Dr. Seselj needed had not taken place yet, and so we informed Dr. Seselj that we would be willing to try to schedule an interview again after this medical treatment was completed. And we are still willing to do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I put the question and I raised the matter not because the Trial Chamber or I as a Pre-Trial Judge has any right at all to get involved in -- in this. It's something that is exclusively within the discretion of Dr. Seselj or Professor Seselj and you. When I say "you," it's the Office of the Prosecutor or the Prosecutor herself. And I have absolutely nothing to do with that. I raised the matter also because I was informed at least that the presence -- I wasn't aware of the problem that Mr. -- that Dr. Seselj raised with regard to one of his legal advisors. As it was put to me, it was that there was a problem and that you were insisting that the standby counsel be -- be present. I would -- not I as a Pre-Trial Chamber -- would not insist on the standby counsel to be present for such an encounter, for such a meeting unless he think that is he ought to be present. But looking at his terms of appointment, I don't see how -- how he fits in if the accused doesn't want him to fit in. So keep that in mind. That is my personal opinion as a Pre-Trial Judge. I don't think the presence or the absence of Mr. Lazarevic ought to constitute a -- an obstacle. So I will leave it at that, making it clear that I am until no way trying to interfere in what is exclusively the domain of the accused and the Prosecution. But I think if you both think that a meeting between the Prosecutor and the accused can be of some kind of -- of some kind of assistance or a positive step forward, then my recommendation is to go ahead with it. Which brings me, Professor Seselj, to something that I am going to be quite abrupt upon. And I have no intention of crossing swords with you on it, but it's a matter that has been put to you already by -- by my predecessor and also by some decisions, including a decision that I gave myself a few days ago, a couple of days ago, on your application or your motion number 21, and that is your insistence to be assisted by the two persons that you mentioned in your motion, that is Madam Maja Gojkovic and Mr. Slavko Jerkovic. The Rules are what they are. The Rules of the Tribunal do not allow anyone - and there are decisions in other cases - this is not something that is happening only in your case. In the Sljivancanin case, for example, Sljivancanin wanted to bring forward as his legal advisors two lawyers from -- from Serbia, from Belgrade. Initially both were not acceptable to the Registrar, and the Rules insist that you cannot -- you as an accused, Mr. Sljivancanin as an accused, Mr. Radic as an accused, and whoever, no one has the right to come here and say, "This is going to be my lawyer in these proceedings." It did -- doesn't work like that. This Tribunal has got its own Rules, which may be good, which may be bad, but we are bound by them. There is Rule 44, which I am sure you are more than familiar with. Stick to it. If you want either Ms. Gojkovic or Mr. Jerkovic as your legal counsel, there is a procedure to be followed. I cannot authorise either of them to be present here unless they have been approved by the Registrar. You may not like the Registrar. You may not Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. like the Rule. You may feel aggrieved. You may feel that your rights for -- to be represented by counsel of your choice are not being respected, but those are the Rules. They have been applied in other cases. I am here to defend you and to make sure that you have a fair trial from beginning to end, and that doesn't mean just the trial. It also means the pre-trial stage. And every day that passes in between the Pre-Trial Status Conferences. And I can promise you that I will do my best to make sure that your rights are respected. But you must also stick to the Rules. There are lawyers who -- who asked to be the representatives of the accused and were accepted, and there are lawyers who for reasons that the Registrar indicated in his decision were not accepted. And there is a remedy for that. When it came to Sljivancanin, for example, the Registrar refused both of them. I advised Mr. Sljivancanin, Colonel Sljivancanin myself to file an appeal direct to the President of the Tribunal, President Meron, which he did. And the decision of the Registrar was revoked and the matter was referred back to him and one of the two has been appointed, pending -- temporarily at least, pending the finalisation of the whole -- of the whole process. But please, don't try to make things difficult for you first and foremost. If there is a Rule, stick to it, even if you don't like that Rule, even if you think it is against your basic rights. It's that Rule. Challenge the Rule if you want. You have every right to challenge the Rule, and there will be a decision if you try to challenge the Rule. But until you challenge the Rule and until you try to -- to file an application seeking the recognition and acceptance of these two persons as your counsel, I can do nothing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have filed several motions to regulate the status of attorneys Maja Gojkovic and Slavko Jerkovic as my legal advisors or assistants. The term is immaterial. The last time Judge Schomburg tried to make an issue of the terminology because I nominated Maja Gojkovic as my legal advisor and Slavko Jerkovic as my legal assistant. I don't care whether they are called assistants or advisors. In these proceedings, I am defending myself. I am making use of my right under the Statute and the Rules. The Rules do not envisage when an accused is defending himself -- yes, I'll slow down. The Rules do not envisage in cases where an accused is defending himself whether or not he has the right to be assisted by legal assistants in the courtroom or other places connected to the court. However, my legal advisors are not bound to fulfil all the conditions that they would have to fulfil were they my counsel, including knowledge of the English language and the ability to read documents in English. They are only my assistants and they are prepared to meet all their obligations, i.e. safeguarding the confidentiality of documents, protection of witnesses, and everything else that legal assistants and members of Defence teams are bound to do. The Registry has never told me that this is rejected. The Registry is silent on this issue. I wrote to the Registry about ten times, as far as I can recall. Two or three times they gave me only pro forma answers, but mostly they failed to respond. I don't know how a senior legal officer can write to me and say that my objections to the indictment and so on cannot be taken into consideration. I don't understand this. This is not according to the Rules or the Statute. There is a gap here in the law which has to be filled by logical interpretations or, rather, by analogy. And in this case, it would say that if the OTP has the right to have two or three people sitting at their bench, then of course the accused may have two people sitting next to him to assist him. When I came into this courtroom, I didn't even have time to take out all my books, put all my documents in order. There are many things here I need assistance with. I need technical assistance while I am defending myself before this Tribunal. This technical assistance and legal assistance, to avoid being misunderstood -- legal and technical assistance can be given to me by people whom I trust. I trust Maja Gojkovic. She was my Defence counsel on several occasions during trials in Belgrade. I have the book here, "Given Milosevic's main political convict". Maja Gojkovic was my Defence counsel during several proceedings. I also wish to tender this book on this occasion, because the OTP will find elements in it to refute what they say about a joint criminal enterprise in the indictment. Milosevic, Kadijevic, Adzic, and many others cannot be linked up to me. I have proof here that Maja Gojkovic represented me on several occasions before courts. I also have proof in Slavko Jerkovic, in this other book about the faculty of law, also acted as my counsel on several occasion before courts in Belgrade. I am used to cooperating with them during court proceedings. They don't have to be my counsel here, and therefore they don't have to meet the requirement that they speak English. They are the people I understand best and who understand me best. They have already helped me. They helped me to draw up this report under Rule 67, which I will now hand to the OTP. This is 67(A)(ii)(b). I am preparing a special defence, and I explain here what I mean by my special defence and therefore I am addressing you, Your Honour, not the OTP directly so they can object. This is a report on my special defence, and I am adducing to this 80 published books of mine. My expert team has been doing good work. I am pleased with them. I give them suggestions other the phone as to how they should work. I have to pay for these telephone conversations myself. I don't have the right to privileged telephone conversations with them, as other accused have. And these are problems I'm facing. But I am still preparing thoroughly for the proceedings. Therefore, I insist that this issue be resolved, and this is the only way in which it can be resolved. It can also be resolved in another way: The Registry can refuse to approve the appointment of my legal advisor and my legal assistant. They can do that under your Rules. The Court may confirm their decision. I can therefore be reduced to the position of an individual. But then at least I have the right to inform the public of what they have done to me. They won't give me assistants. They won't give me advisors. They won't give me a team. I have to do everything on my own in my cell. If this Tribunal finds it -- agrees to have this kind of public image, then all right. I would like to cooperate with Maja Gojkovic and Slavko Jerkovic. You can accept or reject this. In other case, I will continue to represent myself, as I have started. But the public has a right to know what has been done. They have the right to know that I have to oppose this enormous international machinery all on my own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Professor Seselj, I will just refer you to my decision of the 27th October, which I suppose you have been -- you have a copy of, you have been served with. This was the Trial Chamber's decision on your motion number 21. And I refer you to the paragraph which specifies that if you in addition or in recognition of your right to represent yourself, to present yourself, you require further legal assistance, there is a special procedure that needs to be followed. Follow that procedure, please. And it will go through all the channels; first Registrar. If the Registrar doesn't accept, then there is a remedy; you can go straight either to Trial Chamber or to -- or to the President of the Tribunal, depending on the basis of the -- of the Registrar's decision. But if there is Rule 44, go to that Rule and follow the procedure that is laid in there, because otherwise we will continue like this. You continue complaining, and maybe to an extent you are right in that anyone who decides to -- to defend himself like -- like you have is -- is depriving himself from the useful, sometimes less useful, assistance by -- by counsel. But if you -- if you had decided not to defend yourself, you would have had counsel, co-counsel, and assistant. You have a right to defend yourself. But you must also be prepared to carry the responsibilities, which you obviously are prepared to -- to carry. And you also have a right to have some kind of assistance, but you have to follow the -- the adequate procedure. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. So please, I am going to stop this matter now here, leave it at that. This is my message to you: There is a special procedure. There is a special Rule. Can I ignore that Rule because of what you said? Even if you have 100 per cent right, I still cannot ignore the Rule. And then there is the final thing that I want to make clear to you, that everyone here has got his or her own compartment. I as the Pre-Trial Judge or I as Presiding Judge of the Trial Chamber have got -- I have got a limited jurisdiction. I cannot interfere into the jurisdiction of the Prosecutor or into your -- in your rights, and I cannot interfere in the jurisdiction of -- of the Registrar. The Rules provide a remedy for most instances, not always because there is discretion and discretion. But in this matter, please refer to Rule 44 and stick to that Rule and have a decision by the Registrar, which you then can appeal if you don't like. All right? Let's move to something else. I don't really have anything else to raise myself, unless you want to raise any further matter. And I start with the Prosecution. Is there any other matter that you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the only other matter at hand for the Prosecution this morning, Your Honour, is to -- with the assistance of the representative of the registrar to provide this material to Dr. Seselj under Rule 68. And we have two receipts that we would ask him to sign, one for him to keep, one for the Prosecution's records, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I suppose there is no objection on your part to sign such a receipt, Professor Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. There are -- is there any other matter that you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. Professor Seselj, before I conclude, and there are a few minor matters that I would like to ask you about, to make sure that you are being dealt with as -- as you should. Would you like to raise any matter related to your state of health?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Please go ahead. One moment. Do you prefer to say it in open session, or do you want to go into private session?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only in public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But Your Honour, you didn't ask me whether I had any other status issues to raise, as you asked the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I will go into that after going into my health? Yes. Recently I had a thorough medical checkup, so I would like to inform you of the results. First, the result of my blood test; there were no problems. Secondly, my urine test; also no problems. Everything is normal. X-ray of the lungs; no danger. My blood pressure is 135/80. Blood test for Hepatitis B; negative. For Hepatitis C; negative. For AIDS; negative. For the coxaci virus; negative. My EEG shows nervousness of the heart caused by the frustrations and the psychological sufferings I am undergoing looking at your robes, Your Honour. I insisted that the Judges should wear, at least in my proceedings, normal civilian clothes, because I am terribly irritated by your Roman Catholic inquisitorial clothing. I insist on this. I don't think Judge Schomburg understood me and took me seriously. I have lost 18 kilogrammes because of my psychological frustration due to your robes. I don't know how else to explain it. My health problem when I arrived in the Detention Unit, I had been an active sportsman. I had been playing football, and I had -- I had ruptured my muscle in my stomach. And now I can feel all my intestines with my fingers. I have been waiting for an operation for three months. An operation is the only way of resolving this problem. Living with this problem for three months is not easy. I am beginning to think that this perhaps is intentional, because the operation takes only about an hour. All my tests and checkups are all right, so this is no reason not to have the operation. Is this how General Djordje Djukic, Dr. Milan Kovacevic, General Momir Talic and Slavko Dokmanovic were killed? They all died because they did not receive medical assistance on time. In my case, I'm not dead yet, but I can see what the intention behind this is. Why do I have to wait for months for a relatively simple operation? At least in my country it's relatively simple. Had I been arrested as the worst criminal in Belgrade, I would not have had to wait more than a week in the central prison to have this operation. I have the impression that I am being tortured intentionally. Perhaps I'm wrong. Perhaps you have other information. Perhaps you don't see this as a serious problem. For me at present there is no problem more serious than this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And with regard to other conditions of your detention, do you have any complaints? Are you otherwise treated well in the Detention Unit?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the Detention Unit staff, they treat me and everybody else quite correctly. I have no objections. But at the last Status Conference, Judge Schomburg promised me a bookshelf. I'm having a lot of problems with books and documents and so on, and this problem has not been solved yet. I have to tell you this. I don't have any other problems in the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... When I said that, there are a few minor things that I am coming to myself, that is one of them. In fact, I wanted to make sure that you have had this bookshelf installed, put in place, and obviously it hasn't happened. Now, Madam Registrar, I want you to block the entire part of the accused's response or remarks on his state of health and conditions of detention, copy it, and paste it and send in an official manner to the commandant of the Detention Unit with an order from the Tribunal directing him to furnish the Trial Chamber with his remarks on Dr. Seselj's complaints, to be filed within -- by not later -- by not later than Friday - by not later than Friday - the date of Friday would be what, Mr. Von Hebel? Today is the 29th, no?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's the 31st.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The 31st. Friday, the 31st. And the understanding is that if in the opinion of the Trial Chamber the matter that has been raised by Dr. Seselj needs to be dealt with by the Trial Chamber itself, then an extra additional sitting of a Status Conference or a fresh Status Conference will be held next week to have a clear picture of what exactly is happening and for any provision that the Trial Chamber might need to take. In particular, the Trial Chamber would like to have a full medical report relating to the condition that Dr. Seselj in his statement states needs to be attended to surgically. So the position is as follows: By Friday, I should have a full report from the commandant. If it is necessary, we will have another Status Conference next week, if I need more information or if I see that things haven't been going as they should. If matters can be solved without the need of a Status Conference, then obviously they will be solved without the need of a Status Conference. Next week I have sittings in the morning and sittings in the afternoon, starting from 9.00 until 7.00 -- 9.00 in the morning until 7.00 in the evening, but if necessary we will find time to fit in an extra Status Conference to deal with your health -- your health condition. There were two minor things before I give you again the floor, in case you have other -- other matters that you would like to raise. The bookshelf; I have a note here and which frankly I understand part of it. I don't understand the second part. Bookshelf is needed for your cell, I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. am told. And now today you're telling me that you haven't -- since the last Status Conference you haven't been provided with this bookshelf?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Schomburg promised that I would get a bookshelf at the last Status Conference, but I haven't got it yet. I'm still waiting for it. And this is causing me a lot of problems. Everything is in chaos. There are books and documents everywhere, all over the place. And the cell is not that roomy. I've thrown out all the ballasts from the cell. I've thrown out the ventilator, everything I could throw out. But I don't have enough room in there. It would help me to get better organised for the proceedings. And these are shelves such as exist in the prison already, in the detention unit, but they're not in the cells yet. So I need to have at least the minimum conditions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. What I am informed is that this will be supplied when the appropriate procedure is followed and the ZATF [phoen] form - I don't know what it is - is completed by the accused requesting a bookshelf. Between -- since the last Status Conference, did you fill in a form asking for a shelf or anything or -- I mean, you have to tell me. I'm not in a position to know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The form requesting such things, there is no such form in the Detention Unit. I told the chief to -- about this orally, and he told me that he could not provide me with a bookshelf because then he would have to provide one for every accused. There is no form for this type of request. It doesn't exist. There is a form for certain types of requests. Each type of request has its own form, but nothing like this has happened before, so there is no form for it. Your Honour, where there is goodwill, forms are not so important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Again, my directive is, Madam Registrar, that again this part of the transcript be copied and sent to the commandant of the Detention Unit with a recommendation to look into this matter and ensure that the accused is supplied with the necessary furnishings, be it a bookshelf or whatever, that would put some order -- that would enable him to put some order to his -- to his documentation. This is what happens when you write too many books, Professor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, apparently it's a good thing that I wrote so many books, because they will help me to oppose this indictment, because everything is in the books.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. There was also another thing: Again, I mean, I am just mentioning this because I want to hear it from your mouth, but you -- are you still objecting to having anything to do with computers and use of a laptop?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never raised any objection. I simply refused to use those things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why do you refuse to use those things?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I have the very negative experience before me of other accused and their Defence counsel. Your Honour, I knew at least a month in advance that I would be indicted here, and I talked to other lawyers and other accused when I arrived here. The Prosecution is creating such chaos with disks that are not in good order or have various kinds of computer programmes on them, that they have to use a lot of time and energy in order to use all this. Secondly, I have only a basic rudimentary knowledge of computers. I can type with ten fingers. But I am not so expert in the use of computers that I can solve any problem that arises. So I don't want to go into it. Secondly, I am perhaps old-fashioned, and it's easier for me to concentrate when holding a pen and a paper than staring into a computer screen. It makes my eyes hurt. I can look into a computer screen for perhaps an hour or two at the most, but I can spend 10 or 12 hours with books and papers. So this is not capricious on my part. Maybe Judge Schomburg explained it different last time, so -- well, I will not use this. I will use the means that I feel are necessary and can be useful for me and serve their basic purpose. I also complained about the lighting, but I solved this on my own. My wife brought me cables and lamps, and now I have all these wires all over my cell. I had to solve this in a very primitive manner, but I have solved it. She was unable to bring me a bookshelf, however.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. But I -- I still hope that by time I will convince you that you can, with your intelligence and your practical approach, learn how to use a computer and you will see for yourself the great advantages, even that there are -- even in preparation of your own defence. I'm pretty sure that if I ask the commandant to provide for lessons to be given to you in the use of a computer, the fact that you only use ten fingers would be no obstacle. And being old-fashioned as -- as you put it, is no obstacle at all. These are easy things, and you can learn how to make good use of a laptop for all -- for a multitude of purposes within -- within a day or two. It's so easy. I'm pretty sure that someone of your calibre of -- a professor with your intelligence -- it's like when I wanted to ride a horse the first time. I was told, "Listen, look at the others. They all know how to learn -- they all know how to ride a horse. Why do you think it's difficult?" And I tried it, and it was easy. You will see that it will be easy for you to -- once you decide to give it a try. Now, last but not least, is there any other matter that you would like to raise? And you have half an hour, if you need half an hour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just have one question to ask. No, I won't need that much time, no. Your Honour, I once tried to ride when I was ten years old and I fell off the horse. If you continue to conduct the proceedings in this correct manner, there will be no procedural problems as far as I am concerned, because I think that you have behaved very correctly today in these proceedings. As far as the computer is concerned, my decision is definite. I have already organised things in my own way, and I work in the most efficient way I can. My sight is not very good, and that prevents me from working with a computer. I know the basic functions; I know how to use the Internet, et cetera. That's not a problem. But it's not possible for me to spend a long time at a computer. There is another serious problem that I would like to raise at the Status Conference. I have already submitted a written submission to the Trial Chamber requesting the permission to be visited by Vladika Milesevski and Bishop Filaret. These are some of the most -- he is one of the most prominent Orthodox persons, and he's in the bishopry where the Sveti Sava cemetery is located, the Milesevo monastery, which for the Serbian people has great mythical, religious, and spiritual importance. I've already addressed Mr. -- Judge Schomburg, and I think that his response should be re-examined by this Trial Chamber, since according to Rule 70 on the Rules of Detention, it says that not a single -- not a single -- according to Rule 63, I wouldn't be allowed to receive visits, and this can be seen in Rule 66, that attempts -- it claimed that there could be bad influence, that there could be influence on other proceedings, et cetera. There is no reason to prevent the bishop Filaret from visiting for these reasons. They're reasons which don't have to do with the court. The European Union, in the case of Bishop Filaret, who has great authority, forbade him from entering the territory of the European Union. Since this court is exterritorial, I think that I should be granted permission to have the Bishop Filaret visit me, since I know that as the main religious body of the Orthodox Church, that they have decided to support this claim and they have taken certain diplomatic moves to make it possible for Bishop Filaret to visit me. I assume in such a case he would visit all the other Serbs who were detained in The Hague Tribunal. This is something that would be very important for me. I insist that I have the right to this, according to the Rules on Detention, and I will not refrain from making such a claim. This is of great importance for all the other detainees. They have been regularly visited by priests here. They have been visited by other bishops, who are also prominent from Western Europe, from Montenegro, et cetera. But I insist on Archbishop Filaret being allowed to visit me. This would be very significant for all The Hague Tribunal detainees, given that he is a prominent man and someone who by virtue of his authority could give spiritual strength to all the detainees. Naturally, I'm not authorised to insist on this, on behalf of all the other detainees. I'm insisting on this on my behalf. But I would also like to inform you that his presence would be much appreciated by all the other Serbs who are detained here. And I insist on this religious right and this right is guaranteed by virtue of international conventions too, and this right would be respected in all the prisons and courts in my country. No one would attempt to deprive me of this right there, and I insist on being granted this right here too. Why is the name of the Archbishop Filaret on the list of persons being prevented from entering the European Union? Well, because he is a great authority in the Orthodox Serbian Church, and the international community, et cetera, all those who are against the Serbian Church are preventing him from coming here, and this is why I insist that he should be allowed to come here and that he should be enabled to perform a religious ceremony with the Serbs who respect him and who are members of the Serbian Orthodox Church. I know that this is a test for The Hague Tribunal at the whole. And Your Honour, since you have conducted yourself in a very Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. serious way in these proceedings, I think that you will attempt to have this right of mine granted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Professor Seselj, I certainly want first and foremost to assure you that I attach to this matter great importance, but I also need to draw your attention to the fact that the Trial Chamber, as previously composed, that is, by Judge Schomburg, myself, and Judge Mumba, on the 30th of September, in response -- or following your motion number 19, which included inter alia a request to -- to have -- to have Bishop -- His Eminence Bishop Filaret visit you and to attend to your religious needs, there was a decision taken on the 30th of September which decided that you certainly have a right to meet with a representative of your religion but there is nothing under the international human rights law that would justify your claim to have a specific religious officer or dignitary to attend to your religious needs. I am informed that you were served with a copy of this decision on the 3rd of October, that's the 3rd of this month. I do not have an indication here in the documentation that I have that you have filed an appeal. Have you appealed against -- against this decision?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, such a decision is not a procedural decision. Such a decision is taken on an ad hoc basis, and it can be modified on an ad hoc basis by the same Trial Chamber or, rather, the Pre-Trial Chamber in this case. To the extent that I mention these issues, you will decide on this. Certain circumstances have changed in the meantime. And if I now object and then ask for permission to appeal against this decision, I don't find this right. To ask for the Pre-Trial Chamber to allow me to appeal their decision, yet they took the decision. This is against legal principles, and I have already mentioned this in my objection, which concerns the collision between the Rules and the Statute. But that's another issue. Your Honour, this is a request that I will incessantly insist on. You can take a new decision with regard to that matter, regardless of the fact that the previous decision was such as it was. Because this is not a procedural issue, which would mean that procedural matters have to be respected in this case. This is a problem that has arisen in the course of my life in the Detention Unit. This problem can be solved one way and tomorrow in another way. One day you can solve the problem by opening the window and the next day by putting up the heating. That is something that concerns my life. You can decide whether it should be done from the point of view of general legal principles and from the point of view of international norms. And naturally, in the case, from the point of view of the interests of justice so that the spiritual life of detainees be satisfied. If this isn't contrary to Rule 66 of the detention rules, if there's no danger of fleeing, of posing a danger, et cetera, et cetera, I won't go into everything that is cited under this Rule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Professor Seselj, again, I will not cross swords with you on this, because my -- my task is not to discuss with any of the parties but to decide on the issues that are submitted. The procedure to be followed is not what you are suggesting. The fact that this may have nothing to do with procedural law or procedural practice is irrelevant. The procedure that needs to be followed is: If you're not happy with -- you're not satisfied with any of the decisions that the Trial Chamber gives, the remedy is to appeal. It's true that sometimes there is certification needed by the Trial Chamber itself before you can actually appeal, but I am promising you that dealing with a matter like this, if you ask for certification, I will grant it and the matter will go to the appeal. But don't ask me to revoke contrario imperio the decision that the Trial Chamber has taken already based on the arguments that you are presenting now, which are basically the same arguments which the Trial Chamber turned down. So what you need is to present the case to a new Court, a new Trial Chamber, that is the Appeals Chamber. There is -- I think you are still in time. And even if you aren't, there is a solution. And I can promise you that I consider the matter of great importance and I will grant you certification so the matter can go to the Appeals Chamber and then they will decide whether it's -- you have any strength in -- or value in your arguments or whether it's the arguments of the Trial Chamber contained in the decision of the 30th September which hold water, which are valid. So this is my suggestion. Don't ask me to revoke a decision that has already been taken by the Trial Chamber, if there is a remedy that is provided for by the Rules themselves. I can promise you, as I repeat, that if you ask for certification, certification will be granted. In other words, authorisation to proceed with -- with filing an appeal.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, does this mean that you have now authorised me to appeal? Because oral authorisation is just as valid as a written authorisation. If you have authorised me to do it, this I will write such an appeal immediately today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. Unfortunately, the authorisation has to be signed not just by me but also by the two other Judges composing the Trial Chamber, and therefore I need an application. But I can assure you that there will be certification forthcoming, because I see no reason why certification should be rejected or -- or deprived, refused on something which is so fundamentally important. So do file a very short, one-page application for certification stating only that this is a matter of -- which is of fundamental importance to you, because it attaches to one of the fundamental rights that is acknowledged by -- amongst other, the European Convention on Human Rights, and certification will follow. Even if there has been -- if the -- even if the time limit has lapsed. I can promise you that. But I can't grant you certification orally now when the decision was taken by the Trial Chamber collegially. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anything else you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As the Prosecution has handed over its material before you here, I would like you to tell the registry that they should take over the material that I have prepared for the Prosecution, pursuant to Rule 67. If they could take charge of this material. I think it should be done in the same manner. They don't even have to sign. The fact that you are present here is sufficient for me. But they should be given this material. They should be provided with this material. This material consists of 294 pages, and I'm informing the Prosecution of my intention to carry out -- conduct a special defence, pursuant to Rule 67, and also that they should take charge of these 80 books of mine. And the three books that I have brought here, that I've mentioned today, I would like this to be tendered to the Court, because I will be referring to these books in the course of the trial. So this has to do with "The trials of the restless vojvoda." Then this other book here, and the book on Milosevic, "Political Convict." This is going to be important because my defence will be founded on refuting the Prosecution's claim that it concerns a joint criminal enterprise, which involves myself, Milosevic, and many others. So these books are not for the Prosecution. This is for the Chamber. And the 80 books and material that I have, the registry should take charge of this material and hand it over to the Prosecution, pursuant to an order issued by you, I will not address them directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Professor Seselj. Okay. So the two books -- perhaps Professor Seselj can indicate them more precisely to us with the title of the book, so that we don't confuse the other books with the books that you are handing over to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: These are the two books which are bound in white. If you have the --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are the three books, hard-cover books, and this is for the record: "The Ottoman Turncoats," and "The trials of the restless vojvoda." These three books are for the record, for the Court. And the 80 books, perhaps I could be assisted, and they should be provided to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution does not object to Dr. Seselj tendering these three books to the Trial Chamber at this time. The Prosecution would simply ask that it also receive a copy of these books as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And I think that is a fair statement on the part of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Copies of these three books? We can do that at the next Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not urgent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And I would also ask you for something else, Professor Seselj, which I usually do when -- when either of the two parties - in the Brdjanin case, I've had books coming from all directions, as you can imagine - and usually the approach is as follows: There will be parts from the book that are more important than others. There will be parts that you will not be making use of. But there will be parts that you will be relying upon almost on a daily basis as we go on. My invitation to you as from now is to isolate and indicate those parts from the book that you definitely will be referring to and making use of as we Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. go along so that we have them translated at an early stage. Because as you can imagine, I don't understand the language and I cannot possibly have an interpreter sit here with me and translate verbally those three volumes to me, because my -- my term of office will come to an end before the exercise is concluded. So what I suggest is that you isolate these parts as -- when you have time so that we can have them translated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have completed this task as far as the 80 books are concerned. This text here -- in this text, I refer to certain parts of these books. These are my public addresses in parliament, public discussions on radio, television, et cetera, everything that in fact forms the essence of the indictment. All of this has been covered, and it won't be difficult at all for the Prosecution to find their way here. Very professional lawyers have processed this for my needs, lawyers from my defence team. So this task has been completed. It's not a task that I have performed for the three books I have mentioned, but when it is necessary, when the time comes, I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Work on it. Work on it. Take your time and work on it, on the three books. All right? Because the Prosecution has -- has got the service of staff members of the Prosecution -- of the Office of the Prosecution who speak the language, but I don't. I mean, I -- I have to rely on interpreters. So I think we can bring this session to an end.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will this material be taken charge of, Your Honour? It will. Very good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand that you are going to hand it over to the Prosecution or that it will be -- you will make it available to the Trial Chamber, which will make it available to the Prosecution. And the understanding is that this notice or document giving notice of special defence that you are tendering, that I will at least have the courtesy of a copy of it. I don't know if I really have the right under the Rule itself, because the Rule mentions notice to be given to the Prosecution, not necessarily to the Trial Chamber, but I would appreciate if I have a copy of it once it is in your possession.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. We have not received anything yet. But as far as we do, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But I take it that you are going to receive it. So that means this Status Conference comes to an end here. If necessary, depending on the response from the commandant of the Detention Unit, if necessary we'll have another Status Conference next week. If not, the next Status Conference will be held within the statutory time limit of 120 days. And I am sure that Professor Seselj will -- will let me know when the time is ripe for the next Status Conference, as he did for the purpose of this Status Conference. So the -- we stand adjourned until the next Status Conference, whenever that will be, if it's next week or -- or in four months' time. I thank you.
